questions.text: In Strided Local Attention , each token attends only to a local window of neighbors. While this reduces computational complexity to [IMAGE: /data/images/da5004_2026T1_ET_AN_p2_Im6.webp|inline] (linear in ), what is a significant limitation of a single layer of such attention?

It requires more memory than full attention.
It cannot be parallelized on GPUs.

questions.correct_answer: It has a limited receptive field and cannot capture long-range dependencies directly.

questions.text: A transformer layer with absolute positional encoding and another with ALiBi are compared on sequences extended from length 128 to 512, without retraining. Which numerical behavior is most likely for ALiBi in this extrapolation scenario?
options: Attention scores remain numerically well-shaped because ALiBi biases scale linearly with distance, not with a fixed maximum length.
The model cannot compute positional information beyond 128 because ALiBi stores one embedding per absolute position up to 128 only.
ALiBi attention becomes undefined for positions beyond 128 because its biases require precomputed lookup tables that stop at 128.
Attention scores collapse to near zero for distant positions because ALiBi uses fixed sinusoidal patterns tied to the original length 128.
questions.correct_answer: Attention scores remain numerically well-shaped because ALiBi biases scale linearly with distance, not with a fixed maximum length.

questions.text: Select the statements that correctly distinguish fine-tuning from zero-shot prompting for GPT-style models.
options: In Fine-Tuning, the weights of the pre-trained model (and often a new specific head) are updated using backpropagation on a labeled dataset.
In Zero-Shot Prompting, the model weights are frozen (not updated); the task is formulated purely through the design of the input text (prompt).
Zero-Shot Prompting generally achieves higher accuracy than Fine-Tuning when abundant labeled data is available.
Fine-Tuning typically requires a task-specific output layer (like a linear classifier), whereas Zero-Shot Prompting relies on the model generating text directly.
correct_answer: In Fine-Tuning, the weights of the pre-trained model (and often a new specific head) are updated using backpropagation on a labeled dataset.
In Zero-Shot Prompting, the model weights are frozen (not updated); the task is formulated purely through the design of the input text (prompt).
Fine-Tuning typically requires a task-specific output layer (like a linear classifier), whereas Zero-Shot Prompting relies on the model generating text directly.

questions.text: Why do standard LLM architectures include explicit Positional Encodings (like RoPE or Sinusoidal) despite the causal mask providing some implicit order?

questions.text: Consider Multi-Query Attention (MQA) . How does its architecture differ from standard Multi- Head Attention (MHA) to improve inference efficiency?
options: It uses multiple query heads but only a single attention head.
It maintains multiple Query heads but shares a single Key and Value head across all Query heads.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about fine-tuning strategies such as gradual unfreezing and multi-task learning in the context of the T5 model are correct?
options: In gradual unfreezing, layers are progressively unfrozen starting from the task-specific (top) layers toward the input (bottom) layers.
Multi-task learning in T5 typically improves performance uniformly across all tasks.
Multi-task pre-training (as used in T5) followed by task-specific fine-tuning often performs better than relying on multi-task learning alone.
Gradual unfreezing can help mitigate catastrophic forgetting of pre-trained representations during T5 fine-tuning.
correct_answer: In gradual unfreezing, layers are progressively unfrozen starting from the task-specific (top) layers toward the input (bottom) layers.
Multi-task learning in T5 typically improves performance uniformly across all tasks.
Gradual unfreezing can help mitigate catastrophic forgetting of pre-trained representations during T5 fine-tuning.

questions.text: Select all correct statements regarding Local Attention Variants (like Sparse, Dilated, or Windowed Attention).
options: Many local attention variants reduce complexity toward linear with sequence length.
They always outperform full attention on all tasks, regardless of sequence length.
Stacking multiple layers of local attention increases the effective receptive field, similar to dilated convolutions in CNNs.
They can be combined with global tokens (e.g., in BigBird) to ensure some tokens can attend to the entire sequence.
correct_answer: Many local attention variants reduce complexity toward linear with sequence length.
Stacking multiple layers of local attention increases the effective receptive field, similar to dilated convolutions in CNNs.
They can be combined with global tokens (e.g., in BigBird) to ensure some tokens can attend to the entire sequence.

questions.text: Which of the following techniques are used in Flash Attention to speed up attention computation and save memory?
options: Tiling: Breaking the large matrices into smaller blocks that fit into the fast SRAM.
Recomputation: Recomputing the attention matrix during the backward pass instead of storing it in HBM.
Approximation: Using a low-rank approximation of the attention matrix to avoid exact calculation.
Kernel Fusion: Fusing multiple operations (MatMul, Mask, Softmax, Dropout) into a single kernel to reduce memory reads/writes.
correct_answer: Tiling: Breaking the large matrices into smaller blocks that fit into the fast SRAM.
Recomputation: Recomputing the attention matrix during the backward pass instead of storing it in HBM.
Kernel Fusion: Fusing multiple operations (MatMul, Mask, Softmax, Dropout) into a single kernel to reduce memory reads/writes.
